expectations.text: Defines a TypeScript TemplateSpec type/interface (e.g. extends Lightning.Component.TemplateSpec) rather than typing the whole class as any

The class then wires it via `extends Lightning.Component<ButtonTemplateSpec> implements Lightning.Component.ImplementTemplateSpec<ButtonTemplateSpec>` (lines 18-21). `TemplateSpecLoose` (the any-like opt-out) is not used, and no property or method is typed `any`.

expectations.text: Template child refs (Background, Label) use PascalCase and are distinguished from camelCase properties (onEnter, label) per Lightning's TS conventions

The original button.js already used this casing for its tag names, and the executor preserved it rather than renaming anything.

claims.claim: The original button.js only had setters for `label` and `onEnter`, with no getters, meaning reading `button.label` back would silently return undefined
claims.evidence: Confirmed against skills/lightningjs-v2-conventions/evals/files/button.js: only `set onEnter(cb)` (line 26) and `set label(value)` (line 30) exist; there is no `get label()` or `get onEnter()`.

claims.claim: `_handleEnter()` should not carry the `override` keyword because it is picked up by Lightning's key-dispatch naming convention rather than being a declared method on the Lightning.Component base class
claims.evidence: references/focus-and-input.md documents that the 'Handle phase' searches for `_handle{KeyName}()` by name convention (lines 95-97) and its checklist separately lists `_handleEnter()` as an action-key convention (line 125), consistent with it not being a literal base-class override.

claims.claim: The conversion introduces no observable behavior change other than making `label`/`onEnter` genuinely readable
claims.evidence: Diffing outputs/Button.ts against button.js: same default template dimensions/colors (300x80, 0xff2b2b2b / 0xff4b9fff), same `_init` reset of onEnter to null, same patch calls in `_focus`/`_unfocus`/`set label`, same `_handleEnter` guard logic. claims.claim: Background/Label are children created in _template() and never removed, justifying the class-field + `!` pattern over a getter-per-access pattern
claims.evidence: button.js's `_template()` (and the converted Button.ts's) always includes both `Background` and `Label` unconditionally with no code path that removes them, matching the rule of thumb in references/typescript.md ('Child is created in _template() and never removed -> assign once as a class field with !').
